translation_notes: Identity translation: `triple` is a whole triple PATTERN held as an opaque caller-supplied string -- upstream's own checkEntailments(g) calls this with three shapes: ':Carl :hasChild :Ann .', ':Ann rdf:type :Child .', ':Juliet :hasChild :Ann .' -- concatenated with `+` straight into the ASK query's body: `"""ASK {""" + triple + """ }"""`.

Same limit as the sibling lab4 region (city-knowledge-graphs/python@lab4/RDFSReasoning.py, same function name, near-identical body): out of reach by construction on the read side -- querying.md is explicit that s{ }'s interpolation ({expr}) 'is allowed where a term may stand' and lowers to initBindings, never a string substitution. There is no island for 'an entire triple pattern held in a variable', the same limit INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 notes for -{ }/m{ } (which take a WRITTEN pattern, never one received as data), here on rdflib's own query engine rather than a BGP island. Subject, predicate and object vary independently across the three call sites, so there is no fixed term slot to interpolate even after the fact.

checkEntailment(g, triple) only prints (no return, no assertion); it is the three real (g, triple) invocations from upstream's checkEntailments(g), against a hand-written fixture graph, that prove the (unmodified) region still computes right: one ASK comes back True (triple1), two come back False -- the zero-solution case for this stratum (triple2, triple3). fixture.ttl documents which and why; it does not attempt to reproduce owlrl's OWL 2 RL closure (that reasoning step belongs to the enclosing OWLRLInference(), which is not part of this region).
